name.text: Finding the mistake in a combined transformation

questiontext.text:
Achieng wants the single matrix for the [[if test="is(t1=\"rx\")"]]reflection in the x-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(t1=\"ry\")"]]reflection in the y-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(t1=\"ryx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(t1=\"rmyx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = -x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(t1=\"r90\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise about O[[/if]][[if test="is(t1=\"r180\")"]]rotation of \(180^\circ\) about O[[/if]][[if test="is(t1=\"r270\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) clockwise about O[[/if]] followed by the [[if test="is(t2=\"rx\")"]]reflection in the x-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"ry\")"]]reflection in the y-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"ryx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"rmyx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = -x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"r90\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise about O[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"r180\")"]]rotation of \(180^\circ\) about O[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"r270\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) clockwise about O[[/if]], and the final image of \(K({@k[1]@},\,{@k[2]@})\). Her working has exactly one mistake.

  1. Matrix of the first transformation: \(A = {@A@}\).
  2. Matrix of the second transformation: \(B = {@Bs@}\).
  3. The single matrix is [[if test="is(er=3)"]]\(A \times B\)[[else]]\(B \times A\)[[/if]].
  4. [[if test="is(er=3)"]]\(A \times B\)[[else]]\(B \times A\)[[/if]] \(= {@Ps@}\).
  5. Final image of K: \(({@img[1]@},\,{@img[2]@})\).

(a) Which step has the mistake?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Give the correct single matrix.

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
(a) [[if test="is(er=1)"]][[/if]][[if test="is(er=2)"]]The mistake is in Step 2. The matrix of the [[if test="is(t2=\"rx\")"]]reflection in the x-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"ry\")"]]reflection in the y-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"ryx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"rmyx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = -x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"r90\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise about O[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"r180\")"]]rotation of \(180^\circ\) about O[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"r270\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) clockwise about O[[/if]] is \({@B@}\), not \({@Bs@}\). Steps 3 to 5 then follow from the wrong matrix.[[/if]][[if test="is(er=3)"]]The mistake is in Step 3. The first transformation's matrix goes on the right, so the single matrix is \(B \times A\), not \(A \times B\).[[/if]][[if test="is(er=4)"]][[/if]][[if test="is(er=5)"]]The mistake is in Step 5. The matrix in Step 4 is right, but the image is the matrix times the column of K: \({@Ps@}{@kc@} = {@ta.kc@}\).[[/if]]

(b) \(BA = {@B@}{@A@} = {@ta@}\), and the final image of K is \(({@tk[1]@},\,{@tk[2]@})\).

questiondescription.text:
Matrices and Transformations: finding the mistake in a combined transformation

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.1: Find the wrong step in working for the single matrix of two successive transformations, and give the correct matrix.

Core

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: Step 4 correctly multiplies the matrices it is given, row by column. Check the other steps one at a time: the two matrices, the order, then the image of K.

Step 1 is right: \({@A@}\) is the matrix of the [[if test="is(t1=\"rx\")"]]reflection in the x-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(t1=\"ry\")"]]reflection in the y-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(t1=\"ryx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(t1=\"rmyx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = -x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(t1=\"r90\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise about O[[/if]][[if test="is(t1=\"r180\")"]]rotation of \(180^\circ\) about O[[/if]][[if test="is(t1=\"r270\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) clockwise about O[[/if]].

falsefeedback.text: [[if test="is(ans1=\"s2\")"]]Step 2 is right: \({@B@}\) is the matrix of the [[if test="is(t2=\"rx\")"]]reflection in the x-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"ry\")"]]reflection in the y-axis[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"ryx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"rmyx\")"]]reflection in the line \(y = -x\)[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"r90\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) anticlockwise about O[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"r180\")"]]rotation of \(180^\circ\) about O[[/if]][[if test="is(t2=\"r270\")"]]rotation of \(90^\circ\) clockwise about O[[/if]]. [[/if]][[if test="is(ans1=\"s3\")"]]Step 3 is right: the first transformation's matrix goes on the right, so the single matrix is \(B \times A\). [[/if]][[if test="is(ans1=\"s5\")"]]Step 5 is right for the matrix in Step 4: \({@Ps@}{@kc@} = {@Ps.kc@}\). [[/if]]Check each step: the two matrices, then the order (second \(\times\) first), then the arithmetic.

truefeedback.text: That is \(A \times B\)[[if test="is(er#5)"]], which is also the matrix in Achieng's working[[/if]]. The first transformation's matrix goes on the right: \(B \times A\).

falsefeedback.text: Write the matrix of each transformation, then multiply (second) \(\times\) (first), row by column.
